EGY.hook: About 95% of Egyptians live on roughly 5% of the land — from orbit the inhabited country is a thin green ribbon along the Nile.
EGY.place: The northeast corner of Africa, with the Sinai peninsula reaching across into Asia.
EGY.borders: Britain drew the straight 22nd-parallel line with Sudan in 1899, then bent an administrative line around it in 1902 — creating the still-disputed Halayib Triangle and Bir Tawil, the rare land that neither country wants.

DZA.hook: The largest country in Africa, and about four-fifths of it is Sahara — the population clings to the northern coast.
DZA.place: The middle of the Maghreb coast between Morocco and Tunisia, running deep south into the desert.
DZA.borders: France governed the Sahara from Algiers and drew the desert lines to match, which is why Algeria swells so deep into the desert; the Moroccan line was left vague enough to cause the 1963 Sand War, and it has been closed since 1994.

SDN.hook: Has more pyramids than Egypt — around 200 of them at Meroë, steeper and narrower, and far less visited.
SDN.place: Below Egypt on the Red Sea, above South Sudan, where the Blue and White Niles meet at Khartoum.
SDN.borders: The Anglo-Egyptian condominium's 1899 lines — the 22nd parallel in the north, colonial survey lines around the rest; the south departed in 2011 along the old internal north–south administrative line, with Abyei still unassigned.

MAR.hook: You can stand on its coast and see Spain — the Strait of Gibraltar is only about 13km across at its narrowest.
MAR.place: The northwest corner of Africa, with both Atlantic and Mediterranean coasts and the Atlas range inland.
MAR.borders: The Algerian line was never fully settled under France — hence the 1963 Sand War; south of the 27°40′ line it holds Western Sahara, the former Spanish colony it annexed after the 1975 Green March, whose status the UN still lists as undecided.

LBY.hook: The Great Man-Made River pumps fossil water from under the Sahara through 2,800km of pipe — the largest irrigation project ever built.
LBY.place: On the Mediterranean between Tunisia and Egypt, almost entirely desert behind a thin coastal strip.
LBY.borders: Three Ottoman-then-Italian provinces — Tripolitania, Cyrenaica, Fezzan — boxed in by straight colonial lines; its claim to Chad's Aouzou Strip, based on an unratified 1935 treaty, was ended by the world court in 1994.

TUN.hook: Contains the northernmost point in Africa, and Carthage — Rome's great rival — stood just outside the modern capital.
TUN.place: The small wedge on the Mediterranean between Algeria and Libya, reaching closest to Sicily.
TUN.borders: Roughly the Ottoman beylik of Tunis, fixed under the French protectorate — the oldest and most stable outline in the Maghreb, with only the southern desert wedge added by French survey lines.
